coverage.note: Built from headlines and RSS descriptions published between 08:00 on Friday and 08:00 on Monday Copenhagen time, from 132 feeds at seventeen publishers. The feeds were not polled for this edition, so nothing published after 20:41 on Sunday was read. Danish outlets decide what is news; international titles are linked where they cover the same story. Nothing else was read.

copy.headline: Britain and Norway welcome the Greenland agreement

extended.text: Britain and Norway welcome the agreement between Greenland, Denmark and the US, the British prime minister's office said, according to Reuters. Andy Burnham and Jonas Gahr Støre, the British and Norwegian prime ministers, met in Liverpool on Sunday, at the Labour conference.

Denmark, Greenland and the US entered into the agreement on Tuesday 22 September. It amends and extends the 1951 defence agreement, confirms the Kingdom of Denmark's sovereignty over Greenland and recognises the Greenlandic people's right to self-determination.

The US may set up defence areas at Narsarsuaq and Mestersvig and expand Pituffik Space Base, formerly the Thule base; other sites need Danish and Greenlandic approval. The agreement opens the way for the US Golden Dome missile defence in Greenland and restricts investment in sensitive sectors from countries outside the EU and NATO.
It has no fixed end date. After signing, it must be approved first by Inatsisartut, Greenland's parliament, and then by the Folketing.
Political forces and American money men are still trying to increase their influence in the far north, a leading US analyst tells DR.

copy.headline: Uber Eats leaves its couriers to pay their own tax

standard.text: Uber Eats runs a model in which its couriers carry the full responsibility for their own tax, according to documents Berlingske has seen, while its competitor Wolt has been forced by the authorities to withhold tax from couriers' pay.
An expert quoted by Berlingske calls the arrangement 'bold' and warns that couriers risk large tax bills. Uber denies that anything is wrong with its tax model.

copy.deck: Wolt has been made to withhold tax from couriers' pay; an expert warns Uber's couriers of large tax bills.

lede.text: Uber Eats leaves its couriers with full responsibility for their own tax, documents seen by Berlingske show, while Wolt has been forced to withhold it; Uber denies anything is wrong.

copy.headline: Germany urges Russia to drop its 'course of escalation' at the first ministers' meeting since 2022

standard.text: Germany's foreign minister, Johann Wadephul, urged Russia to abandon its 'course of escalation' with Germany, Europe and NATO when he met Sergei Lavrov in New York, an unnamed German official told AFP on Saturday. It was the two countries' first foreign ministers' meeting since Russia began the war in Ukraine in 2022.
Wadephul made clear that incidents such as the recent attempted attack in Leipzig would not shake Germany's support for Ukraine, the official said.
Lavrov told the UN that Russia is not interested in war with Europe and that Europe is the one preparing for it. A peace researcher tells DR the meeting is 'very surprising'.
